topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Biology and Lecture Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, welcomes students from different backgrounds, and outlines the key learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a Disruption of Normal Differentiation and Tissue Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer initiates through accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal multicellular differentiation and tissue architecture.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Histology of Tumor Progression, Invasion, and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from contained benign states to invasive and metastatic malignancies, using histological features and colorectal cancer as a primary model.

topics.label: Principles of Tumor Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and exceptions used to name benign and malignant neoplasms across different tissue lineages.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Illness and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how local primary tumor mass effects and widespread metastatic dissemination lead to clinical illness and patient death.

topics.label: Tumor Incidence Across Human Tissues and Comparative Animal Taxa
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the epidemiological frequency of different tumor types in humans and their comparative occurrence across diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Clinical Screening and Early Detection Strategies for Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, histological targets, and practical challenges of population screening and early detection across different cancer types.

topics.label: Concluding Remarks and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by directing students to review the learning outcomes ahead of practical sessions and future classes.
